text:
Alex K: heads-up: scheduling a tenant-probe + gradual evacuation window for eu-west GPU pool next Tue 03:00-04:00 UTC. Purpose: run probe-only traffic for selected tenants, validate egress throttling, and exercise graceful cordon/drain of ephemeral GPU nodes. High-level plan below.

Maria S: is this hitting tenant traffic or only synthetic probes? any cost impact?

Alex K: only synthetic probes for now (tenant-alpha, tenant-beta — non-prod). We'll scale probe qps to mimic typical 95th perc load. Cost: small blip from extra probe traffic + short-lived backfill; estimated additional infra cost ~$120 for the window.

Jamal R: what's the evacuation cadence? how many nodes and what's the expected capacity loss?

Alex K: pool is 64 GPUs. We'll cordon 4 nodes every 10 minutes (cohort size = 4 -> ~6.25% capacity per step). Total planned node cordons: 12 nodes over 90 minutes if we keep going, but for this window we'll only do first 6 nodes (30 min actual cordon time, then hold). Fallback thresholds: if queue depth or P99 latency increases >20% vs baseline, we pause and uncordon.

Li Chen: cache warmup? prefix/KV cache cold starts are the main source of tail spikes.

Alex K: good call. We'll run prefix-warmup from probe-runner before cordoning each cohort. Sequence per cohort: 1) run prefix-warmup, 2) shift probe traffic to cohort-exposed paths for 5min, 3) cordon+drain, 4) observe for 10min.

ops-bot: calendar event created: "eu-west tenant-probe + gradual evac" Tue 03:00-04:00 UTC (organizer: Alex K). :white_check_mark:

Jamal R: can we fallback cross-region if things get bad? routing change is expensive during peak.

Alex K: policy is to use local fallback first (dedicated eu-west spare pool) with cost-tag fallback:eu. Only if local spare <10% and P99 > threshold do we shift to us-east via smart-routing; that'll add egress and inter-region cost — last resort. We'll add a temporary route weight: eu-west:80 -> us-east:20, and monitor.

Maria S: any infra commands we should be ready with?

Alex K: keeping these handy in the runbook slack thread. main ops commands:
```
# cordon cohort by label
rbctl nodes cordon --pool eu-west-gpu --selector cohort=probe-1
# drain gracefully (evict tasks, allow 10m graceful shutdown)
rbctl nodes drain --selector cohort=probe-1 --grace-period 10m
# uncordon if we abort
rbctl nodes uncordon --selector cohort=probe-1
```

Li Chen: probe-runner curl example for prefix warmup?

Alex K: use probe-runner-bot endpoint; sample: 
```
curl -X POST https://probe-runner.internal/api/run \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROBE_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"tenants": ["tenant-alpha"], "prefixes": ["login:", "search:" ] , "qps": 50, "duration_s": 300 }'
```

probe-runner-bot: scheduled probe jobs will post status updates in this thread.

Maria S: what about billing tags so finance can correlate the small bump?

Alex K: we'll tag fallback and probe traffic with cost center tags: `probe-window:3899999999`, `fallback:eu-west` and add a short note to billing.ops ticket.

Jamal R: can we run a quick preflight tomorrow (light ramp) to verify the probe-runner credentials and routes?

Alex K: yes — preflight tomorrow 14:00 UTC, 10 min test. Ops oncall please stand by. @Jamal R @Li Chen @Maria S

Li Chen: i'll prepare the prefix set and warmup script. also will capture KV-cache hit rates pre/post.

ops-bot: oncall schedule shows SRE-oncall: Jamal R for the preflight window.

Alex K: final action items: 1) Li prepare prefix warmup + scripts, 2) probe-runner to schedule probe jobs, 3) Maria update billing tag and notify finance, 4) Jamal monitor oncall and validate routing failover playbook. We'll post runbook link in this thread 1h before window.

Maria S: LGTM.

Jamal R: 👍 I'll be there for the preflight.

Alex K: thanks all — will post runbook link and canary tenants list in the thread tomorrow. :rocket:
